Trace sanitization: gitleaks-based secret redaction.\n//!\n//! Sanitizes trace content before writing to disk by applying vendored gitleaks\n//! rules and workspace-specific custom patterns. Certain structured fields are never redacted regardless of entropy or regex:\n//! - Bead IDs (`needle-*`)\n//! - The token `[REDACTED:...]` itself (already sanitized output)\n//!\n//! ## Custom patterns\n//!\n//!     toml::from_str(toml_str).context(\"failed to parse gitleaks TOML\")?;\n\n        let global = config.allowlist.unwrap_or_default();\n        let global_stopwords: HashSet<String> = global\n .iter()\n            .filter_map(|r| {\n                let normalized = normalize_regex(r);\n                Regex::new(&normalized)\n                    .map_err(|e| {\n Ok(Sanitizer {\n            rules,\n            global_stopwords,\n            global_allowlist_regexes,\n            safe_passthrough,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Sanitize a string, replacing MIN_LINE_LEN {\n            return text.to_string();\n        }\n\n        let trailing_newline = text.ends_with('\\n');\n        let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();\n        let sanitized = lines\n            .iter()\n            .map(|line| self.sanitize_line(line))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\"\\n\");\n\n        if trailing_newline {\n            sanitized + line.to_string();\n        }\n\n        let mut result = line.to_string();\n        for rule in &self.rules {\n            result = self.apply_rule(rule, &result, line);\n        }\n        result\n    }\n\n    fn apply_rule(&self, rule: &CompiledRule, text: &str, original_line: &str) -> String {\n        // Keyword pre-filter: if the rule declares keywords and none appear in\n        // the       return text.to_string();\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut result = text.to_string();\n        let mut scan_start = 0usize;\n\n        loop {\n            // Search in the remaining tail of `result`.\n            let haystack = &result[scan_start..];\n            let caps = match rule.regex.captures(haystack) {\n                Some(c) => c,\n                None => break,\n            };\n\n            let full_match = caps.get(0).unwrap();\n\n            // Determine which group holds the secret.\n            let secret_match = if rule.secret_group > 0 && rule.secret_group < caps.len() {\n                caps.get(rule.secret_group)\n            } else if caps.len() > 1 {\n                // Default: use group 1 when available.\n                caps.get(1)\n            } else {\n                caps.get(0)\n            };\n\n            let secret_m = match secret_match {\n                Some(m) => m,\n                None => {\n                    scan_start += full_match.end();\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            let secret_str = secret_m.as_str();\n\n            // Entropy gate: skip low-entropy strings (placeholders, env var names).\n            if let Some(threshold) = rule.entropy_threshold {\n                if shannon_entropy(secret_str) < threshold {\n                    scan_start += full_match.end();\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Global stopwords (lowercased comparison).\n            let secret_lower = secret_str.to_lowercase();\n            if self.global_stopwords.contains(&secret_lower) {\n                scan_start += full_match.end();\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Global allowlist regexes checked against the secret.\n            if self\n                .global_allowlist_regexes\n                .iter()\n                .any(|r| r.is_match(secret_str))\n            {\n                scan_start += full_match.end();\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Known-safe passthrough: bead IDs, already-redacted strings.\n            if self.safe_passthrough.is_match(secret_str.as_bytes()) {\n                scan_start += full_match.end();\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Per-rule allowlist checks.\n              RegexTarget::Match => full_match.as_str(),\n                    RegexTarget::Line => original_line,\n                };\n                if al_re.is_match(subject) {\n                    allowed = true;\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if allowed {\n                scan_start += full_match.end();\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Per-rule stopwords.\n            if rule.allowlist_stopwords.contains(&secret_lower) {\n                scan_start += full_match.end();\n                continue;\n            }\n\n secret_m.start();\n            let abs_secret_end = scan_start + secret_m.end();\n            let abs_full_end = scan_start + full_match.end();\n\n            result = format!(\n /// Returns statistics about how many rules were skipped by the\n    /// Aho-Corasick keyword pre-filter (i.e., rules whose keywords\n    /// were not found in the text, allowing them to be skipped\n    /// without running the expensive regex).\n    pub fn measure_skip_stats(&self, text: &str) -> SkipStats {\n        let mut total_checks = 0usize;\n        let mut skipped_by_keywords = 0usize;\n\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfn compile_rule(spec:        _ => {}\n248\t                            }\n249\t                        }\n250\t                    }\n251\t                }\n252\t            }\n253\t\n254\t            _ => {}\n255\t        }\n256\t    }\n257\t\n258\t    /// Produce a `VariantComparison` for every template that has been observed.\n259\t    pub fn comparisons(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, VariantComparison> {\n260\t        self.stats\n261\t            .iter()\n262\t            .map(|(template_name, by_version)| {\n263\t                let comparison = VariantComparison {\n264\t                    template_name: ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n287\t// Percentile helpers\n288\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n289\t\n290\t/// Calculate the median (50th percentile) from a slice of values.\n291\t///\n292\t/// The median is the value separating the higher half from the lower half of a data sample.\n293\t/// For an odd number of elements, it's the middle value. For an even number, it's the\n294\t/// average of the two middle values.\n295\t///\n296\t/// # Edge Cases\n297\t///\n298\t/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n299\t///\n300\t/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n301\t/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n302\t/// - **Even number of elements**: Returns the average of the two middle values\n303\t///\n304\t/// # Examples\n305\t///\n306\t/// ## Basic usage\n307\t///\n308\t/// ```\n309\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_median;\n310\t///\n311\t/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50];\n312\t/// let median = calculate_median(&latencies);\n313\t/// assert_eq!(median, 30); // Middle value\n314\t/// ```\n315\t///\n316\t/// ## Even number of elements\n317\t///\n318\t/// ```\n319\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_median;\n320\t///\n321\t/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40];\n322\t/// let median = calculate_median(&latencies);\n323\t/// assert_eq!(median, 25); // Average of 20 and 30\n324\t/// ```\n325\tpub fn calculate_median(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n326\t    if latencies.is_empty() {\n327\t        return 0;\n328\t    }\n329\t\n330\t    let n = latencies.len();\n331\t    if n == 1 {\n332\t        return latencies[0];\n333\t    }\n334\t\n335\t    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n336\t    sorted.sort();\n337\t\n338\t    let mid = n / 2;\n339\t    if n % 2 == 1 {\n340\t        // Odd number of elements: return middle value\n341\t        sorted[mid]\n342\t    } else {\n343\t        // Even number of elements: return average of two middle values\n344\t        (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2\n345\t    }\n346\t}\n347\t\n348\t/// Calculate the 95th percentile from a slice of values.\n349\t///\n350\t/// The 95th percentile (p95) is the value below which 95% of observations\n351\t/// fall. It is commonly used to understand the \"tail\" of a distribution\n352\t/// — for example, in latency metrics, p95 tells you that 95% of requests\n353\t/// completed within this time, while the slowest 5% took longer.\n354\t///\n355\t/// # Edge Cases\n356\t///\n357\t/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n358\t///\n359\t/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n360\t/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n361\t/// - **Two elements**: Uses linear interpolation to estimate p95 between the two values\n362\t/// - **Small samples (2-3 elements)**: Linear interpolation provides a reasonable estimate\n363\t///\n364\t/// All edge cases return sensible results without panicking.\n365\t///\n366\t/// # Algorithm\n367\t///\n368\t/// This function uses **linear interpolation**, which is the same method\n369\t/// used by Criterion.rs and is more accurate than the nearest-rank method:\n370\t///\n371\t/// 1. If the slice is empty, return 0 (no data case)\n372\t/// 2. If the slice has one element, return that element\n373\t/// 3. Sort the values in ascending order\n374\t/// 4. Calculate the rank: `rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of elements\n375\t/// 5. Split the rank into integer and fractional parts\n376\t/// 6. Return the linear interpolation: `floor_value + (ceiling_value - floor_value) * fraction`\n377\t/// 7. Round to the nearest integer for the final result\n378\t///\n379\t/// This method was chosen because:\n380\t/// - **Accurate**: Uses linear interpolation like Criterion.rs for smooth percentile estimates\n381\t/// - **Standard**: Matches the behavior of common benchmarking libraries\n382\t/// - **Well-documented**: The algorithm is described in statistical literature\n383\t/// - **Deterministic**: Always produces the same result for the same input\n384\t/// - **Handles all sample sizes**: Works correctly from 0 to very large datasets\n385\t///\n386\t/// Note: This uses linear interpolation, not nearest-rank. For example, with 10 elements\n387\t/// `[10, 20, ..., 100]`, the 95th percentile is approximately `95.5` (rounded to `96`),\n388\t/// not the maximum value `100`.\n389\t///\n390\t/// # Examples\n391\t///\n392\t/// ## Basic usage with sorted data\n393\t///\n394\t/// ```\n395\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n396\t///\n397\t/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100];\n398\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&latencies);\n399\t/// // rank = 0.95 * 9 = 8.55, floor_index = 8, fraction = 0.55\n400\t/// // floor_value = 90, ceiling_value = 100\n401\t/// // interpolated = 90 + 10 * 0.55 = 95.5 → 96\n402\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 96);\n403\t/// ```\n404\t///\n405\t/// ## Works with unsorted input (sorts internally)\n406\t///\n407\t/// ```\n408\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n409\t///\n410\t/// let unsorted = vec![100u128, 10, 50, 30, 70, 40, 60, 20, 80, 90];\n411\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&unsorted);\n412\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 96); // Function sorts internally → same result\n413\t/// ```\n414\t///\n415\t/// ## Larger dataset\n416\t///\n417\t/// ```\n418\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n419\t///\n420\t/// // 20 elements: rank = 0.95 * 19 = 18.05, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.05\n421\t/// let data = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,\n422\t///                  110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200];\n423\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&data);\n424\t/// // floor_value = 190, ceiling_value = 200\n425\t/// // interpolated = 190 + 10 * 0.05 = 190.5 → 191\n426\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 191);\n427\t/// ```\n428\t///\n429\t/// ## Single element (degenerate case)\n430\t///\n431\t/// ```\n432\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n433\t///\n434\t/// let single = vec![42u128];\n435\t/// let p95 = ```\n448\t///\n449\t/// ## Two elements (small sample)\n450\t///\n451\t/// ```\n452\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n453\t///\n454\t/// let two = vec![10u128, 20];\n455\t/// let p95 = 20\n459\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 20); // Linear interpolation estimates p95\n460\t/// ```\n461\t///\n462\t/// ## Three elements (small sample)\n463\t///\n464\t/// ```\n465\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n466\t///\n467\t/// let three = vec![10u128, 20, 30];\n468\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&three);\n469\t/// // rank = 0.95 * 2 = 1.9, floor_index = 1, fraction = ```\n474\t///\n475\t/// ## Real-world latency example\n476\t///\n477\t/// ```\n478\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n479\t///\n480\t/// // Simulated latency data in milliseconds\n481\t/// let recommendations\n495\tpub fn calculate_p95(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n496\t    if latencies.is_empty() {\n497\t        return 0;\n498\t    }\n499\t\n500\t    let n = latencies.len();\n501\t    if n == 1 {\n502\t        return latencies[0];\n503\t    }\n504\t\n505\t    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n506\t    sorted.sort();\n507\t\n508\t    // Linear interpolation method (like Criterion.rs)\n509\t    // Formula: rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1)\n510\t    // For p95: rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)\n511\t    let rank = 0.95 * (n - 1) as f64;\n512\t    let floor_index = rank.floor() as usize;\n513\t    let fraction = rank - floor_index as f64;\n514\t\n515\t    let floor_value = sorted[floor_index];\n516\t    let ceiling_value = sorted[floor_index + 1];\n517\t\n518\t    // Linear integer.\n522\t    // Add a small epsilon to handle floating point precision issues (e.g., 95.5 → 95.4999... → 95).\n523\t    // Standard rounding: 95.0-95.499... → 95, 95.5-96.499... → 96\n524\t    let epsilon = 1e-9;\n525\t    (interpolated + epsilon).round() as u128\n526\t}\n527\t\n528\t/// Calculate the 99th percentile from a slice of values.\n529\t///\n530\t/// The 99th percentile (p99) is ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n711\t\n712\t/// Collector for aggregating samples across multiple benchmark iterations.\n713\t///\n714\t/// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n715\t/// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p95 percentile.\n716\t///\n717\t/// # Statistical Approach\n718\t///\n719\t/// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n720\t/// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single dataset\n721\t/// 2. **Calculate one p95** on the pooled data\n722\t///\n723\t/// **Do NOT average p95 values** from individual iterations — this is statistically\n724\t/// invalid because percentiles are non-linear Averaging them produces\n725\t/// misleading results.\n726\t///\n727\t/// # Example\n728\t///\n729\t/// ```no_run\n730\t/// use needle::stats::P95Collector;\n731\t/// use Instant::now();\n738\t///     // ... perform work ...\n739\t///     collector.record(start.elapsed().as_micros());\n740\t/// }\n741\t///\n742\t/// // Calculate p95 across all iterations\n743\t/// let p95_us = collector.p95();\n744\t/// println!(\"p95 latency: {} μs\", p95_us);\n745\t/// ```\n746\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n747\tpub struct P95Collector {\n748\t    /// All recorded latency            samples: Vec::new(),\n757\t        }\n758\t    }\n759\t\n760\t    /// Create a new collector with pre-allocated capacity.\n761\t    ///\n762\t    /// Use this when you know how many samples self.samples.push(latency_us);\n773\t    }\n774\t\n775\t    /// Record multiple latency samples at once.\n776\t    pub fn record_all(&mut self, latencies: impl IntoIterator<Item = u128>) {\n777\t        self.samples.extend(latencies);\n778\t    }\n779\t\n780\t    /// Calculate the p95 percentile across all recorded samples.\n781\t    ///\n782\t    /// Returns `0` if no samples have been collected samples.\n803\t    ///\n804\t    /// Returns `(min, max, avg)` in microseconds, or `None` if no samples.\n805\t    pub fn stats(&self) -> Option<(u128, u128, f64)> {\n806\t        if self.samples.is_empty() {\n807\t            return None;\n808\t        }\n809\t        let min = *self.samples.iter().min().unwrap();\n810\t        let max = *self.samples.iter().max().unwrap();\n811\t        let sum: u128 = self.samples.iter().sum();\n812\t        let avg = sum as f64 / self.samples.len() as f64;\n813\t        Some((min, max, avg))\n814\t    }\n815\t}\n816\t\n817\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n818\t// Stats engine — multi-dimensional outcome aggregation\n819\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n820\t\n821\t/// Grouping dimension for the `needle stats` command.\n822\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\n823\tpub enum StatsDimension {\n824\t    /// Group by template version tag (e.g., `\"pluck-v2\"`).\n825\t    TemplateVersion,\n826\t    /// Group by template name / task type (e.g., `\"pluck\"`).\n827\t    TaskType,\n828\t    /// Group by worker identifier (e.g., `\"needle-alpha\"`).\n829\t    Worker,\n830\t}\n831\t\n832\t/// Aggregated statistics row for one value of a grouping dimension.\n833\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\n834\tpub struct StatsRow {\n835\t    /// The dimension value (version, task type, or worker id).\n836\t    pub key: String,\n837\t    /// Total number of beads dispatched in this group.\n838\t    pub beads: u64,\n839\t    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Success\"` outcome.\n840\t    pub pass: u64,\n841\t    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Failure\"` outcome.\n842\t    pub fail: u64,\n843\t    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Timeout\"` outcome.\n844\t    pub timeout: u64,\n845\t    /// Sum of (tokens_in + tokens_out) across all effort events in this group.\n846\t    pub total_tokens: u64,\n847\t    /// Sum of `estimated_cost_usd` across all effort events in this group.\n848\t    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n849\t    /// Number of effort events with token/cost data (denominator for averages).\n850\t    pub effort_events: u64,\n851\t}\n852\t\n853\timpl StatsRow {\n854\t    /// Pass rate as a fraction in `[0.0, 1.0]`. `None` when `beads == 0`.\n855\t    pub fn pass_rate(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n856\t        if self.beads == 0 {\n857\t            None\n858\t        } else {\n859\t            Some(self.pass as f64 / self.beads as f64)\n860\t        }\n861\t    }\n862\t\n863\t    /// Average total tokens (in + out) per effort event. `None` when no effort data.\n864\t    pub fn avg_tokens(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n865\t        if self.effort_events == 0 {\n866\t            None\n867\t        } else {\n868\t            Some(self.total_tokens as f64 / self.effort_events as f64)\n869\t        }\n870\t    }\n871\t\n872\t    /// Average cost in USD per effort event. `None` when no effort data.\n873\t    pub fn avg_cost_usd(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n874\t        if self.effort_events == 0 {\n875\t            None\n876\t        } else {\n877\t            Some(self.total_cost_usd / self.effort_events as f64)\n878\t        }\n879\t    }\n880\t}\n881\t\n882\t/// Compute per-group statistics from a pre-filtered slice of telemetry events.\n883\t///\n884\t/// Correlates `agent.dispatched`, `outcome.classified`, and `effort.recorded`\n885\t/// events by `bead_id`, grouping each bead under the chosen `dimension`.\n886\t///\n887\t/// Pass the result of [`telemetry::read_logs`] (already time-filtered) here.\n888\tpub fn compute_stats(\n889\t    events: &[crate::telemetry::TelemetryEvent],\n890\t    dimension: StatsDimension,\n891\t) -> Vec<StatsRow> {\n892\t    use std::collections::HashMap;\n893\t\n894\t    // bead_id → dimension key (populated from agent.dispatched events)\n895\t    let mut bead_key: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();\n896\t    let mut rows: BTreeMap<String, StatsRow> = BTreeMap::new();\n897\t\n898\t    for event in events {\n899\t        match event.event_type.as_str() {\n900\t            \"agent.dispatched\" => {\n901\t                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n902\t                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n903\t                    None => continue,\n904\t                };\n905\t                let key = match dimension {\n906\t                    StatsDimension::TemplateVersion => event\n907\t                        .data\n908\t                        .get(\"template_version\")\n909\t                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n910\t                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n911\t                        .to_string(),\n912\t                    StatsDimension::TaskType => .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n917\t                        .to_string(),\n918\t                    StatsDimension::Worker => event.worker_id.clone(),\n919\t                };\n920\t                bead_key.insert(bead_id, key.clone());\n921\t                let row = rows.entry(key.clone()).or_insert_with(|| StatsRow {\n922\t                    key: key.clone(),\n923\t                    ..Default::default()\n924\t                });\n925\t                row.beads += 1;\n926\t            }\n927\t\n928\t            \"outcome.classified\" => {\n929\t                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n930\t                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n931\t                    None => continue,\n932\t                };\n933\t                if let Some(key) = bead_key.get(&bead_id) {\n934\t                    if let Some(row) = rows.get_mut(key) {\n935\t                        match event.data.get(\"outcome\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n936\t                            Some(\"Success\") => row.pass += 1,\n937\t                            Some(\"Failure\") => row.fail += 1,\n938\t                            Some(\"Timeout\") => row.timeout += 1,\n939\t                            _ => {}\n940\t                        }\n941\t                    }\n942\t                }\n943\t            }\n944\t\n945\t            \"effort.recorded\" => {\n946\t                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n947\t                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n948\t                    None => continue,\n949\t                };\n950\t                if let Some(key) = bead_key.get(&bead_id) {\n951\t                    if let Some(row) = rows.get_mut(key) {\n952\t                        let tokens_in = event\n953\t                            .data\n954\t                            .get(\"tokens_in\")\n955\t                            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n956\t                            .unwrap_or(0);\n957\t                        let tokens_out = event\n958\t                            .data\n959\t                            .get(\"tokens_out\")\n960\t                            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n961\t                            .unwrap_or(0);\n962\t                        row.total_tokens += tokens_in + tokens_out;\n963\t                        if let Some(cost) = event\n964\t                            .data\n965\t                            .get(\"estimated_cost_usd\")\n966\t                            .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())\n967\t                        {\n968\t           _ => {}\n976\t        }\n977\t    }\n978\t\n979\t    rows.into_values().collect()\n980\t}\n981\t\n982\t// /// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n1760\t    /// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p99 percentile.\n1761\t    ///\n1762\t    /// # Statistical Approach\n1763\t    ///\n1764\t    /// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n1765\t    /// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single {\n1782\t    ///     let start = Instant::now();\n1783\t    ///     // ... perform work ...\n1784\t    ///     collector.record(start.elapsed().as_micros());\n1785\t    /// }\n1786\t    ///\n1787\t    /// // Calculate p99 across all iterations\n1788\t    /// let p99_us = collector.p99();\n1789\t    /// println!(\"p99 latency: {} μs\", p99_us);\n1790\t    /// ```\n1791\t    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n1792\t    pub struct P99Collector {\n1793\t        /// All recorded latency samples in microseconds.\n1794\t        samples: Vec<u128>,\n1795\t    }\n1796\t\n1797\t    impl P99Collector }\n1804\t\n1805\t        /// Create a new collector with pre-allocated capacity.\n1806\t        ///\n1807\t        /// Use this when you know how many samples you'll collect to avoid\n1808\t ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Percentile helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Calculate the median (50th percentile) from a slice of values.\n///\n/// The median is the value separating the higher half from the lower half of a data sample.\n/// For an odd number of elements, it's the middle value. For an even number, it's the\n/// average of the two middle values.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n///\n/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n/// - **Even number of elements**: Returns the average of the two middle values\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ## Basic usage\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_median;\n///\n/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50];\n/// let median = calculate_median(&latencies);\n/// assert_eq!(median, 30); // Middle value\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Even number of elements\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_median;\n///\n/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40];\n/// let median = calculate_median(&latencies);\n/// assert_eq!(median, 25); // Average of 20 and 30\n/// ```\npub fn calculate_median(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n    if latencies.is_empty() {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    let n = latencies.len();\n    if n == 1 {\n        return latencies[0];\n    }\n\n    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n    sorted.sort();\n\n    let mid = n / 2;\n    if n % 2 == 1 {\n        // Odd number of elements: return middle value\n        sorted[mid]\n    } else {\n        // Even number of elements: return average of two middle values\n        (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2\n    }\n}\n\n/// Calculate the 95th percentile from a slice of values.\n///\n/// The 95th percentile (p95) is the value below which 95% of observations\n/// fall. It is commonly used to understand the \"tail\" of a distribution\n/// — for example, in latency metrics, p95 tells you that 95% of requests\n/// completed within this time, while the slowest 5% took longer.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n///\n/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n/// - **Two elements**: Uses linear interpolation to estimate p95 between the two values\n/// - **Small samples (2-3 elements)**: Linear interpolation provides a reasonable estimate\n///\n/// All edge cases return sensible results without panicking.\n///\n/// # Algorithm\n///\n/// This function uses **linear interpolation**, which is the same method\n/// used by Criterion.rs and is more accurate than the nearest-rank method:\n///\n/// 1. If the slice is empty, return 0 (no data case)\n/// 2. If the slice has one element, return that element\n/// 3. Sort the values in ascending order\n/// 4. Calculate the rank: `rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of elements\n/// 5. Split the rank into integer and fractional parts\n/// 6. Return the linear interpolation: `floor_value + (ceiling_value - floor_value) * fraction`\n/// 7. Round to the nearest integer for the final result\n///\n/// This method was chosen because:\n/// - **Accurate**: Uses linear interpolation like Criterion.rs for smooth percentile estimates\n/// - **Standard**: Matches the behavior of common benchmarking libraries\n/// - **Well-documented**: The algorithm is described in statistical literature\n/// - **Deterministic**: Always produces the same result for the same input\n/// - **Handles all sample sizes**: Works correctly from 0 to very large datasets\n///\n/// Note: This uses linear interpolation, not nearest-rank. For example, with 10 elements\n/// `[10, 20, ..., 100]`, the 95th percentile is approximately `95.5` (rounded to `96`),\n/// not the maximum value `100`.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ## Basic usage with sorted data\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&latencies);\n/// // rank = 0.95 * 9 = 8.55, floor_index = 8, fraction = 0.55\n/// // floor_value = 90, ceiling_value = 100\n/// // interpolated = 90 + 10 * 0.55 = 95.5 → 96\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 96);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Works with unsorted input (sorts internally)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let unsorted = vec![100u128, 10, 50, 30, 70, 40, 60, 20, 80, 90];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&unsorted);\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 96); // Function sorts internally → same result\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Larger dataset\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// // 20 elements: rank = 0.95 * 19 = 18.05, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.05\n/// let data = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,\n///                  110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&data);\n/// // floor_value = 190, ceiling_value = 200\n/// // interpolated = 190 + 10 * 0.05 = 190.5 → 191\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 191);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Single element (degenerate case)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let single = vec![42u128];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&single);\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 42); // Only value available\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Empty input\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let empty: Vec<u128> = vec![];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&empty);\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 0); // No data → returns 0\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Two elements (small sample)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let two = vec![10u128, 20];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&two);\n/// // rank = 0.95 * 1 = 0.95, floor_index = 0, fraction = 0.95\n/// // floor_value = 10, ceiling_value = 20\n/// // interpolated = 10 + 10 * 0.95 = 19.5 → 20\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 20); // Linear interpolation estimates p95\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Three elements (small sample)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let three = vec![10u128, 20, 30];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&three);\n/// // rank = 0.95 * 2 = 1.9, floor_index = 1, fraction = 0.9\n/// // floor_value = 20, ceiling_value = 30\n/// // interpolated = 20 + 10 * 0.9 = 29.0 → 29\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 29); // Linear interpolation estimates p95\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Real-world latency example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// // Simulated latency data in milliseconds\n/// let latencies = vec![\n///     12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 35, 40,\n///     45, 50, 55, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 120, 150\n/// ];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&latencies);\n/// // rank = 0.95 * 19 = 18.05, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.05\n/// // floor_value = 120, ceiling_value = 150\n/// // interpolated = 120 + 30 * 0.05 = 121.5 → 122\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 122);\n/// ```\n///\n/// # See Also\n///\n/// - [`docs/p95-calculation-algorithms.md`](../../docs/p95-calculation-algorithms.html) — Comprehensive survey of p95 algorithms and recommendations\npub fn calculate_p95(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n    if latencies.is_empty() {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    let n = latencies.len();\n    if n == 1 {\n        return latencies[0];\n    }\n\n    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n    sorted.sort();\n\n    // Linear interpolation method (like Criterion.rs)\n    // Formula: rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1)\n    // For p95: rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)\n    let rank = 0.95 * (n - 1) as f64;\n    let floor_index = rank.floor() as usize;\n    let fraction = rank - floor_index as f64;\n\n    let floor_value = sorted[floor_index];\n    let ceiling_value = sorted[floor_index + 1];\n\n    // Linear interpolation: floor + (ceiling - floor) * fraction\n    let interpolated = floor_value as f64 + (ceiling_value - floor_value) as f64 * fraction;\n\n    // Round to nearest integer.\n    // Add a small epsilon to handle floating point precision issues (e.g., 95.5 → 95.4999... → 95).\n    // Standard rounding: 95.0-95.499... → 95, 95.5-96.499... → 96\n    let epsilon = 1e-9;\n    (interpolated + epsilon).round() as u128\n}\n\n/// Calculate the 99th percentile from a slice of values.\n///\n/// The 99th percentile (p99) is the value below which 99% of observations\n/// fall. It is commonly used to understand the extreme tail of a distribution\n/// — for example, in latency metrics, p99 tells you that 99% of requests\n/// completed within this time, while the slowest 1% took longer.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n///\n/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n/// - **Two elements**: Uses linear interpolation to estimate p99 between the two values\n/// - **Small samples (2-3 elements)**: Linear interpolation provides a reasonable estimate\n///\n/// All edge cases return sensible results without panicking.\n///\n/// # Algorithm\n///\n/// This function uses **linear interpolation**, which is the same method\n/// used by Criterion.rs and is more accurate than the nearest-rank method:\n///\n/// 1. If the slice is empty, return 0 (no data case)\n/// 2. If the slice has one element, return that element\n/// 3. Sort the values in ascending order\n/// 4. Calculate the rank: `rank = 0.99 * (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of elements\n/// 5. Split the rank into integer and fractional parts\n/// 6. Return the linear interpolation: `floor_value + (ceiling_value - floor_value) * fraction`\n/// 7. Round to the nearest integer for the final result\n///\n/// This method was chosen because:\n/// - **Accurate**: Uses linear interpolation like Criterion.rs for smooth percentile estimates\n/// - **Standard**: Matches the behavior of common benchmarking libraries\n/// - **Well-documented**: The algorithm is described in statistical literature\n/// - **Deterministic**: Always produces the same result for the same input\n/// - **Handles all sample sizes**: Works correctly from 0 to very large datasets\n///\n/// Note: This uses linear interpolation, not nearest-rank. For example, with 10 elements\n/// `[10, 20, ..., 100]`, the 99th percentile is approximately `99.1` (rounded to `99`),\n/// not the maximum value `100`.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ## Basic usage with sorted data\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&latencies);\n/// // rank = 0.99 * 9 = 8.91, floor_index = 8, fraction = 0.91\n/// // floor_value = 90, ceiling_value = 100\n/// // interpolated = 90 + 10 * 0.91 = 99.1 → 99\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 99);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Works with unsorted input (sorts internally)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let unsorted = vec![100u128, 10, 50, 30, 70, 40, 60, 20, 80, 90];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&unsorted);\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 99); // Function sorts internally → same result\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Larger dataset\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// // 20 elements: rank = 0.99 * 19 = 18.81, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.81\n/// let data = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,\n///                  110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&data);\n/// // floor_value = 190, ceiling_value = 200\n/// // interpolated = 190 + 10 * 0.81 = 198.1 → 198\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 198);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Single element (degenerate case)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let single = vec![42u128];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&single);\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 42); // Only value available\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Empty input\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let empty: Vec<u128> = vec![];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&empty);\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 0); // No data → returns 0\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Two elements (small sample)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let two = vec![10u128, 20];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&two);\n/// // rank = 0.99 * 1 = 0.99, floor_index = 0, fraction = 0.99\n/// // floor_value = 10, ceiling_value = 20\n/// // interpolated = 10 + 10 * 0.99 = 19.9 → 20\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 20); // Linear interpolation estimates p99\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Three elements (small sample)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let three = vec![10u128, 20, 30];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&three);\n/// // rank = 0.99 * 2 = 1.98, floor_index = 1, fraction = 0.98\n/// // floor_value = 20, ceiling_value = 30\n/// // interpolated = 20 + 10 * 0.98 = 29.8 → 30\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 30); // Linear interpolation estimates p99\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Real-world latency example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// // Simulated latency data in milliseconds\n/// let latencies = vec![\n///     12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 35, 40,\n///     45, 50, 55, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 120, 150\n/// ];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&latencies);\n/// // rank = 0.99 * 19 = 18.81, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.81\n/// // floor_value = 120, ceiling_value = 150\n/// // interpolated = 120 + 30 * 0.81 = 144.3 → 144\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 144);\n/// ```\n///\n/// # See Also\n///\n/// - [`calculate_p95`](fn@calculate_p95) — Calculate the 95th percentile\npub fn calculate_p99(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n    if latencies.is_empty() {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    let n = latencies.len();\n    if n == 1 {\n        return latencies[0];\n    }\n\n    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n    sorted.sort();\n\n    // Linear interpolation method (like Criterion.rs)\n    // Formula: rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1)\n    // For p99: rank = 0.99 * (n - 1)\n    let rank = 0.99 * (n - 1) as f64;\n    let floor_index = rank.floor() as usize;\n    let fraction = rank - floor_index as f64;\n\n    let floor_value = sorted[floor_index];\n    let ceiling_value = sorted[floor_index + 1];\n\n    // Linear interpolation: floor + (ceiling - floor) * fraction\n    let interpolated = floor_value as f64 + (ceiling_value - floor_value) as f64 * fraction;\n\n    // Round to nearest integer.\n    // Add a small epsilon to handle floating point precision issues (e.g., 99.5 → 99.4999... → 99).\n    // Standard rounding: 99.0-99.499... → 99, 99.5-100.499... → 100\n    let epsilon = 1e-9;\n    (interpolated + epsilon).round() as u128\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// P95 aggregation utilities\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Collector for aggregating samples across multiple benchmark iterations.\n///\n/// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n/// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p95 percentile.\n///\n/// # Statistical Approach\n///\n/// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n/// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single dataset\n/// 2. **Calculate one p95** on the pooled data\n///\n/// **Do NOT average p95 values** from individual iterations — this is statistically\n/// invalid because percentiles are non-linear statistics. Averaging them produces\n/// misleading results.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::stats::P95Collector;\n/// use std::time::Instant;\n///\n/// let mut collector = P95Collector::new();\n///\n/// // Run benchmark for 50 iterations\n/// for _ in 0..50 {\n///     let start = Instant::now();\n///     // ... perform work ...\n///     collector.record(start.elapsed().as_micros());\n/// }\n///\n/// // Calculate p95 across all iterations\n/// let p95_us = collector.p95();\n/// println!(\"p95 latency: {} μs\", p95_us);\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct P95Collector {\n    /// All recorded latency samples in microseconds.\n    samples: Vec<u128>,\n}\n\nimpl P95Collector {\n    /// Create a new empty collector.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            samples: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new collector with pre-allocated capacity.\n    ///\n    /// Use this when you know how many samples you'll collect to avoid\n    /// reallocations during benchmarking.\n    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            samples: Vec::with_capacity(capacity),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a single latency sample in microseconds.\n    pub fn record(&mut self, latency_us: u128) {\n        self.samples.push(latency_us);\n    }\n\n    /// Record multiple latency samples at once.\n    pub fn record_all(&mut self, latencies: impl IntoIterator<Item = u128>) {\n        self.samples.extend(latencies);\n    }\n\n    /// Calculate the p95 percentile across all recorded samples.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `0` if no samples have been recorded.\n    pub fn p95(&self) -> u128 {\n        calculate_p95(&self.samples)\n    }\n\n    /// Return the number of samples collected.\n    pub fn count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.samples.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Clear all recorded samples.\n    pub fn clear(&mut self) {\n        self.samples.clear();\n    }\n\n    /// Get a reference to the underlying samples.\n    pub fn samples(&self) -> &[u128] {\n        &self.samples\n    }\n\n    /// Calculate additional statistics on the collected samples.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `(min, max, avg)` in microseconds, or `None` if no samples.\n    pub fn stats(&self) -> Option<(u128, u128, f64)> {\n        if self.samples.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let min = *self.samples.iter().min().unwrap();\n        let max = *self.samples.iter().max().unwrap();\n        let sum: u128 = self.samples.iter().sum();\n        let avg = sum as f64 / self.samples.len() as f64;\n        Some((min, max, avg))\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Stats engine — multi-dimensional outcome aggregation\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Grouping dimension for the `needle stats` command.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum StatsDimension {\n    /// Group by template version tag (e.g., `\"pluck-v2\"`).\n    TemplateVersion,\n    /// Group by template name / task type (e.g., `\"pluck\"`).\n    TaskType,\n    /// Group by worker identifier (e.g., `\"needle-alpha\"`).\n    Worker,\n}\n\n/// Aggregated statistics row for one value of a grouping dimension.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\npub struct StatsRow {\n    /// The dimension value (version, task type, or worker id).\n    pub key: String,\n    /// Total number of beads dispatched in this group.\n    pub beads: u64,\n    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Success\"` outcome.\n    pub pass: u64,\n    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Failure\"` outcome.\n    pub fail: u64,\n    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Timeout\"` outcome.\n    pub timeout: u64,\n    /// Sum of (tokens_in + tokens_out) across all effort events in this group.\n    pub total_tokens: u64,\n    /// Sum of `estimated_cost_usd` across all effort events in this group.\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    /// Number of effort events with token/cost data (denominator for averages).\n    pub effort_events: u64,\n}\n\nimpl StatsRow {\n    /// Pass rate as a fraction in `[0.0, 1.0]`. `None` when `beads == 0`.\n    pub fn pass_rate(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n        if self.beads == 0 {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(self.pass as f64 / self.beads as f64)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Average total tokens (in + out) per effort event. `None` when no effort data.\n    pub fn avg_tokens(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n        if self.effort_events == 0 {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(self.total_tokens as f64 / self.effort_events as f64)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Average cost in USD per effort event. `None` when no effort data.\n    pub fn avg_cost_usd(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n        if self.effort_events == 0 {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(self.total_cost_usd / self.effort_events as f64)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute per-group statistics from a pre-filtered slice of telemetry events.\n///\n/// Correlates `agent.dispatched`, `outcome.classified`, and `effort.recorded`\n/// events by `bead_id`, grouping each bead under the chosen `dimension`.\n///\n/// Pass the result of [`telemetry::read_logs`] (already time-filtered) here.\npub fn compute_stats(\n    events: &[crate::telemetry::TelemetryEvent],\n    dimension: StatsDimension,\n) -> Vec<StatsRow> {\n    use std::collections::HashMap;\n\n    // bead_id → dimension key (populated from agent.dispatched events)\n    let mut bead_key: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();\n    let mut rows: BTreeMap<String, StatsRow> = BTreeMap::new();\n\n    for event in events {\n        match event.event_type.as_str() {\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => {\n                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n                    None => continue,\n                };\n                let key = match dimension {\n                    StatsDimension::TemplateVersion => event\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"template_version\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                        .to_string(),\n                    StatsDimension::TaskType => event\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"template_name\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                        .to_string(),\n                    StatsDimension::Worker => event.worker_id.clone(),\n                };\n                bead_key.insert(bead_id, key.clone());\n                let row = rows.entry(key.clone()).or_insert_with(|| StatsRow {\n                    key: key.clone(),\n                    ..Default::default()\n                });\n                row.beads += 1;\n            }\n\n            \"outcome.classified\" => {\n                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n                    None => continue,\n                };\n                if let Some(key) = bead_key.get(&bead_id) {\n                    if let Some(row) = rows.get_mut(key) {\n                        match event.data.get(\"outcome\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n                            Some(\"Success\") => row.pass += 1,\n                            Some(\"Failure\") => row.fail += 1,\n                            Some(\"Timeout\") => row.timeout += 1,\n                            _ => {}\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            \"effort.recorded\" => {\n                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n                    None => continue,\n                };\n                if let Some(key) = bead_key.get(&bead_id) {\n                    if let Some(row) = rows.get_mut(key) {\n                        let tokens_in = event\n                            .data\n                            .get(\"tokens_in\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                            .unwrap_or(0);\n                        let tokens_out = event\n                            .data\n                            .get(\"tokens_out\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                            .unwrap_or(0);\n                        row.total_tokens += tokens_in + tokens_out;\n                        if let Some(cost) = event\n                            .data\n                            .get(\"estimated_cost_usd\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())\n                        {\n                            row.total_cost_usd += cost;\n                        }\n                        row.effort_events += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    rows.into_values().collect()\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n//
